summary: Two classes of utility that compile, resolve, pass every gate and do not do what their name says — both found while specifying Sheet, both now refused by check:utilities. FIRST: Tailwind v4 reads max-w-<name> from --container-* and falls back to --spacing-*. This system emits no container scale and names its spacing steps sm/md/lg/xl — exactly the container scale's names — so Modal's two sizes, written as max-w-md and max-w-xl, compiled to 12px and 24px caps. min-w-80 beat both and every dialog rendered at 320px whatever its size, measured in Chromium. The sizes now bind to --ui-dialog-width-md (26rem, the 416px the sheet draws) and --ui-dialog-width-lg (40rem, derived), new chrome dimensions following --ui-nav-width's precedent, and the gate rejects a bare spacing step in any w-/h-/min-/max- utility. A second, quieter bug fell out of the same measurement: a max-w-[calc(100vw-2rem)] sat in Modal's class list and had never once applied, because tailwind-merge keeps only the LAST max-width and the size class always followed it. Removed rather than reordered — w-full is what actually holds the dialog inside its containing block. SECOND: v4's scale-*, translate-* and rotate-* write the STANDALONE css properties, not transform, which is why Tailwind's own transition-transform expands to `transform, translate, scale, rotate`. Modal and Popover both wrote transition-[opacity,transform] beside data-[starting-style]:scale-98, so the only property transitioning was opacity and both surfaces snapped to full size — proven with getAnimations() in Chromium, since the class list, the compiled rule and the computed transitionProperty all read exactly as intended. Popover even had a test asserting transitionProperty contained 'transform', which passed for the entire life of the defect: it measured the declaration, not the behaviour. The gate now refuses `transform` in a transition list, and requires an enter/exit scale/translate/rotate to be covered by a transition — scoped to data-[starting|ending]-style on purpose, because Button's press scale is deliberately not eased and a broader rule flagged that considered choice as a defect. Two further gate repairs: check:utilities was reading class names out of COMMENTS, so a comment explaining why max-w-md is wrong would have failed the build; and its prefix list had no inset-x/inset-y, which Sheet was the first component to need. Coverage 536 to 550 utilities.

migration.manual: Modal's size prop now has an effect: md caps at 416px and lg at 640px, where both previously rendered at whatever w-full allowed. A layout that relied on every modal being the same width will change. In your own components, a bare spacing step in a width utility (max-w-md) is now a build error — use a chrome token or an explicit value.
